# Stash

> URL management for humans and agents. Share groups of links as a single,
> stateless URL. The stash payload travels inside the URL itself.

## How share URLs work

A share URL looks like `https://stash.illo.fyi/s/#p=<payload>` (or `#q=` for the
QR/base32 form). The payload lives in the URL **fragment** (`#p=...`), which is
never sent to servers. To read a stash programmatically, take the payload string
(everything after `#p=`) and pass it as the `p` **query** parameter to one of the
decode endpoints below.

Payload format: one prefix character + body.
- `C` / `R` (base64url, from `#p=`): `C` = brotli-compressed msgpack, `R` = raw msgpack
- `D` / `S` (base32, from `#q=`): `D` = brotli-compressed msgpack, `S` = raw msgpack

## Endpoints

### /s (canonical, content negotiation)
The stash viewer page and canonical machine-readable endpoint. When the
payload is passed as a query parameter, `GET /s?p=<payload>` decodes it and
negotiates the output format. **Canonical:** `Accept: application/json`,
`text/markdown`, or `text/plain`. **Fallback:** `?format=json|md|txt`.
Without negotiation it serves the interactive HTML viewer.

### Short-URL endpoints (s.illo.fyi)
For short links created by the MCP server (`stash_create`) or the
`POST /api/stash` API, the same decode is available on the shortener
host `https://s.illo.fyi`:

- `GET /s/<id>` with `Accept: application/json`, `text/markdown`, or
  `text/plain` (canonical content negotiation)
- `GET /s/<id>?format=json|md|txt` (explicit fallback; same precedence
  rules as the viewer)
- Without negotiation, `GET /s/<id>` 302-redirects to the interactive
  viewer with the payload inline
- An unknown `format` value returns `400` JSON
- Legacy suffix routes `GET /s/<id>.json`, `/s/<id>.md`, `/s/<id>.txt`
  still resolve but now 301-redirect to the `?format=` form; they will
  be removed in a future release

`<id>` is a 6-character base32 id (e.g. `AHK7QY`). The same three
output formats (JSON, Markdown, plain URL list) are available as on
the viewer.

## Worked example: URL → JSON → MD

Given a share URL `https://stash.illo.fyi/s#p=Cj0K...` (payload after
`#p=`), the same decoded payload is reachable three ways:

```bash
# 1. JSON via Accept negotiation (canonical)
curl -H 'Accept: application/json' 'https://stash.illo.fyi/s?p=Cj0K...'
# → { "version": 6, "title": "My Tabs", "items": [{ "url": "...", "title": "..." }], ... }

# 2. Markdown via Accept negotiation
curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' 'https://stash.illo.fyi/s?p=Cj0K...'
# → [Example](https://example.com)\n[Other](https://other.com)

# 3. Plain URL list (one per line) via text/plain negotiation
curl -H 'Accept: text/plain' 'https://stash.illo.fyi/s?p=Cj0K...'
# → https://example.com
# → https://other.com

# Fallback: explicit format query parameter
curl 'https://stash.illo.fyi/s?p=Cj0K...&format=json'
```

For short links (e.g. `https://s.illo.fyi/s/AHK7QY`), the same three
shapes are reachable via `?format=json|md|txt` and `Accept` content
negotiation, plus `text/plain`.

## Notes for agents

- **All programmatic reads go through `GET /s?p=<payload>`.** Prefer the
  `Accept` header negotiation; `?format=` is a fallback when headers cannot
  be set. Output is identical data across formats.
- Responses are cached until the payload's expiry timestamp.
- Expired stashes still decode (check `isExpired` in JSON output).
- A 400 means the payload string was malformed or truncated, or the
  `format` parameter value was unknown; re-copy the full payload from
  the share URL or use `format=json|md|txt`.
- Rate limit: ~30 requests/minute per IP, HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 60`.

## MCP

- MCP server (Streamable-HTTP, stateless): `https://s.illo.fyi/mcp`
- Tools: `stash_create` (urls -> short link), `stash_get` (id -> items), `stash_decode` (payload -> items)
- Discovery card: `https://s.illo.fyi/.well-known/mcp-server-card`
- Short links live on the same host: `https://s.illo.fyi/s/<id>`
- Rate limit: ~20 creates/min per IP on `/api/stash`, ~60 req/min on `/mcp`; HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 60`.

A second MCP surface is shipped by the browser extension. It exposes the
local stash library (and the current browser tabs) to an AI agent over a
Chrome runtime port named `portName: "mcp"` — no HTTP, no host. The same
discovery card lists it under `servers[]` as
`{ name: "stash-extension", transport: "extension-port", portName: "mcp" }`
with eight tools (`stash_snapshot_tabs`, `stash_list`, `stash_get`,
`stash_create`, `stash_update`, `stash_delete`, `stash_search`,
`stash_decode`). See the extension package (`apps/extension/lib/mcp/`)
for wiring details.

## Profile-local browser-agent surface (`/stashes`)

`https://stash.illo.fyi/stashes/` is a **profile-local** surface for
browser-class agents that run inside the user's browser profile
(ChromeClaw, NanoBrowser, BrowserOS). It is NOT a fetch endpoint. Use
the trailing-slash form (`/stashes/`) directly — `/stashes` without the
slash 308-redirects to it, costing an extra round trip.

- The page is client-rendered (`client:only="react"`) — a plain
  `curl`/`page.request.get` returns an empty Astro shell and **no
  stashes**.
- **Read all stashes in one shot at `/stashes/?agent=json` (or
  `?agent=markdown`).** Open that URL, wait for `data-stash-status="ready"`
  on `<pre id="agent-export">` (JSON, the canonical `StashExport` shape)
  or `<pre id="agent-export-md">` (Markdown, per `/s` conventions), and
  read its text content. This is the surface that works for DOM-snapshot
  browser agents (BrowserOS-class): it is plain visible text, present in
  the accessibility tree and in any DOM-to-text extraction. **Do not**
  click into individual stash cards to enumerate them — expensive and
  unnecessary, the `?agent=` views already return everything.
- The normal view (no `?agent=` query) also embeds a
  `<script type="application/json" id="stash-local-export"
  data-stash-status="ready">{ "version": 1, "source": "extension",
  "stashes": [...] }</script>` island, but **`<script>` elements are
  invisible to default DOM-snapshot/DOM-to-text tools** in common
  browser-agent runtimes — they get stripped before the agent ever sees
  them. Only tools that read raw HTML (`evaluate_script`, `get_dom`, or
  a Playwright/CDP-driven `page.content()`) can reach it. If your runtime
  only offers a DOM snapshot or extracted page text, use `?agent=json`
  instead — do not rely on this island.
- Unlike the island, which mirrors only the browser-extension library,
  `?agent=json` and `?agent=markdown` serialize everything the signed-in
  profile can see on the page — on a viewer-local-only profile (no
  extension bridge) they return real rows while the island still reports
  `stashes: []`. They always return the same record set as each other.

The rendered list items in the normal view
(`[data-stash-record-id="..."]`, `[data-stash-title]`) are for human
display only: cards render collapsed by default and per-item data only
appears in the DOM once a card is expanded, so agents polling those
selectors at load time will find nothing. Do not rely on them — use
`?agent=json`/`?agent=markdown`.

Stable semantic selectors for browser agents:

- `[data-stash-root]`, `[data-stash-list]` (presence/structure only,
  not a data source)
- `#agent-export`, `#agent-export-md` (JSON/markdown `?agent=` views —
  the recommended read path; lifecycle via their own
  `data-stash-status="loading"|"ready"` attribute)
- `#stash-local-export` (JSON island, normal view; readable only via
  `evaluate_script`/`get_dom`/a Playwright-style `page.content()` — not
  by DOM-snapshot or extracted-text tools; lifecycle via its own
  `data-stash-status="loading"|"ready"` attribute)

This surface is gated on the extension being installed **and** the user
having opted in via `Settings → Local Library Bridge`. Fetch-only agents
must use `/s?p=<payload>&format=json` instead — that endpoint is the
universal baseline and works without the extension.
